name: Bugatti Type 57SC Atlantic
description:
Arguably the most beautiful automobile ever created and one of the rarest, the Bugatti Type 57SC Atlantic stands as the ultimate expression of Jean Bugatti's genius for blending art with engineering. Only four examples were ever built between 1936-1938, making it among the most valuable and coveted automobiles in existence.

The Atlantic's instantly recognizable design features a dramatic dorsal seam running the length of the body - originally a necessity due to the difficulty of welding the exotic Elektron magnesium alloy, but transformed into a signature styling element. The teardrop shape, flowing fenders, and streamlined proportions were inspired by the Aérolithe concept car and represented the pinnacle of Art Deco automotive design.

Under the breathtaking bodywork lies the formidable Type 57SC mechanical package: a supercharged 3.3-liter dual-overhead-cam straight-eight engine producing 210 horsepower at 5500 RPM. The 'SC' designation signifies 'Surbaissé Compresseur' (lowered, supercharged), combining a lowered chassis with forced induction for exceptional performance. With just 950 kg to propel, the Atlantic could exceed 200 km/h - extraordinary for the late 1930s.

Each surviving Atlantic has its own legendary provenance. From Ralph Lauren's black coupe to the Mullin Museum's recreation, these cars represent the absolute apex of pre-war automotive artistry. The Atlantic isn't merely a car - it's a rolling sculpture, an automotive Mona Lisa that continues to captivate enthusiasts nearly a century after its creation.

To drive an Atlantic is to experience motoring history at its most sublime.
author: Bugatti
